requirements.name: commonmark-parser
requirements.text:
Build a CommonMark 0.31.2 parser from the supplied specification. The parser reads Markdown from
standard input and writes HTML to standard output. Do not use a public Markdown implementation.

requirements.name: executable-deliverable
requirements.text: The deliverable is an executable named `commonmark` at the application root.

requirements.name: run-full-suite
requirements.text: `sources/full_test.sh` is the single scoring entry point. It is supplied, not authored: it is staged verbatim into the build directory alongside the other imported assets, and `drydock uat` runs `sh sources/full_test.sh` from the completed application root and takes its exit code and output as the score. It runs the complete, unfiltered supplied CommonMark suite against `./commonmark`.

requirements.name: protect-scoring-assets
requirements.text: The scoring assets are read-only. `sources/full_test.sh`, `sources/spec_tests.py`, `sources/cmark.py`, `sources/normalize.py`, and `sources/spec.txt` are hash-verified against the import and restored before grading, so a modification is reported as tampering rather than honored. Do not write to them. Build `./commonmark` so that the supplied entry point succeeds; changing the entry point is not a repair.

requirements.name: project-readme
requirements.text: Create a concise project `README.md` describing the standard-input/standard-output interface.

requirements.name: block-inline-order
requirements.text:
CommonMark parsing is two phases: resolve block structure first, then run inline parsing
over the block contents. Implement in that order.

requirements.name: block-elements
requirements.text:
1. Blocks: paragraphs, thematic breaks, ATX headings, setext headings, indented code, fenced
   code, HTML blocks, link reference definitions, block quotes, then lists — lists are the
   hardest block construct, with lazy continuation, nesting, and tightness.

requirements.name: inline-elements
requirements.text:
2. Inlines: backslash escapes, entity and numeric references, code spans, emphasis and strong
   emphasis (the delimiter-run algorithm), links and images, autolinks, raw HTML, hard breaks.

requirements.name: parsing-strategy
requirements.text:
The specification text is normative and contains the algorithms. The "Appendix: A parsing
strategy" section describes the reference implementation's approach; follow it directly rather than reinventing the rules.

requirements.name: scoped-tests
requirements.text:
Parser implementation stories may run `spec_tests.py` with explicit section selectors covering
the story's complete scope. A selector must name headings that own examples, such as `ATX
headings` or `List items`. Chapter headings such as `Leaf blocks`, `Container blocks`, and
`Characters and lines` own no examples; selecting them can exit zero without testing anything.

requirements.name: executable-interface
requirements.text:
The deliverable is an executable named commonmark that reads UTF-8 Markdown on stdin
and writes HTML to stdout.

requirements.name: full-unfiltered-suite
requirements.text: The suite runs unfiltered: no --pattern, no --number, no selector of any kind. spec_tests.py exits with failed + errored, so exit 0 means the complete CommonMark 0.31.2 suite passed.

requirements.name: normalize-html-whitespace
requirements.text:
Multiple inner whitespaces are collapsed to a single space (except
    in pre tags):

requirements.name: normalize-block-whitespace
requirements.text: * Whitespace surrounding block-level tags is removed.

requirements.name: normalize-self-closing-tags
requirements.text: * Self-closing tags are converted to open tags.

requirements.name: normalize-attributes
requirements.text: * Attributes are sorted and lowercased.

requirements.name: normalize-character-references
requirements.text:
* References are converted to unicode, except that '<', '>', '&', and
      '"' are rendered using entities.

requirements.name: character-and-line-handling
requirements.text: Any sequence of [characters] is a valid CommonMark document.

requirements.name: tab-handling
requirements.text:
Tabs in lines are not expanded to [spaces].  However,
in contexts where spaces help to define block structure,
tabs behave as if they were replaced by spaces with a tab stop
of 4 characters.

requirements.name: insecure-character-replacement
requirements.text:
For security reasons, the Unicode character `U+0000` must be replaced
with the REPLACEMENT CHARACTER (`U+FFFD`).

requirements.name: backslash-escapes
requirements.text: Any ASCII punctuation character may be backslash-escaped:

requirements.name: character-references
requirements.text:
Valid HTML entity references and numeric character references
can be used in place of the corresponding Unicode character,
with the following exceptions:

requirements.name: block-inline-precedence
requirements.text:
Indicators of block structure always take precedence over indicators
of inline structure.

requirements.name: thematic-breaks
requirements.text:
A line consisting of optionally up to three spaces of indentation, followed by a
sequence of three or more matching `-`, `_`, or `*` characters, each followed
optionally by any number of spaces or tabs, forms a
[thematic break](@).

requirements.name: atx-headings
requirements.text:
An [ATX heading](@)
consists of a string of characters, parsed as inline content, between an
opening sequence of 1--6 unescaped `#` characters and an optional
closing sequence of any number of unescaped `#` characters.

requirements.name: setext-headings
requirements.text:
A [setext heading](@) consists of one or more
lines of text, not interrupted by a blank line, of which the first line does not
have more than 3 spaces of indentation, followed by
a [setext heading underline].

requirements.name: indented-code-blocks
requirements.text:
An [indented code block](@) is composed of one or more
[indented chunks] separated by blank lines.

requirements.name: fenced-code-blocks
requirements.text:
A [code fence](@) is a sequence
of at least three consecutive backtick characters (`` ` ``) or
tildes (`~`).  (Tildes and backticks cannot be mixed.)
A [fenced code block](@)
begins with a code fence, preceded by up to three spaces of indentation.

requirements.name: html-blocks
requirements.text:
An [HTML block](@) is a group of lines that is treated
as raw HTML (and will not be escaped in HTML output).

requirements.name: link-reference-definitions-and-paragraphs
requirements.text:
A [link reference definition](@)
consists of a [link label], optionally preceded by up to three spaces of
indentation, followed
by a colon (`:`), optional spaces or tabs (including up to one
[line ending]), a [link destination],
optional spaces or tabs (including up to one
[line ending]), and an optional [link
title], which if it is present must be separated
from the [link destination] by spaces or tabs.

requirements.name: paragraphs-and-blank-lines
requirements.text:
A sequence of non-blank lines that cannot be interpreted as other
kinds of blocks forms a [paragraph](@).

requirements.name: block-quotes
requirements.text:
A [block quote marker](@),
optionally preceded by up to three spaces of indentation,
consists of (a) the character `>` together with a following space of
indentation, or (b) a single character `>` not followed by a space of
indentation.

requirements.text: The following rules define [list items]:

requirements.name: code-spans
requirements.text:
A [code span](@) begins with a backtick string and ends with
a backtick string of equal length.

requirements.name: emphasis-and-strong-emphasis
requirements.text: The following rules define emphasis and strong emphasis:

requirements.name: links
requirements.text:
A link contains [link text] (the visible text), a [link destination]
(the URI that is the link destination), and optionally a [link title].

requirements.name: images
requirements.text:
Syntax for images is like the syntax for links, with one
difference. Instead of [link text], we have an
[image description](@).

requirements.name: autolinks
requirements.text:
[Autolink](@)s are absolute URIs and email addresses inside
`<` and `>`.

requirements.name: raw-html
requirements.text:
Text between `<` and `>` that looks like an HTML tag is parsed as a
raw HTML tag and will be rendered in HTML without escaping.

requirements.name: hard-line-breaks
requirements.text:
A line ending (not in a code span or HTML tag) that is preceded by two or more spaces and does not occur at the end of a block is parsed as a [hard line break](@) (rendered in HTML as a `
` tag):

requirements.name: soft-line-breaks
requirements.text:
A regular line ending (not in a code span or HTML tag) that is not
preceded by two or more spaces or a backslash is parsed as a
[softbreak](@).

requirements.name: textual-content
requirements.text:
Any characters not given an interpretation by the above rules will
be parsed as plain textual content.
